title: Alignment code says it has no consumers; about thirty modules use it
what: Headers say the alignment reads have no live consumer 'this wave'; about thirty modules import the selectors, several lit in the default preset (RR). Host: src/domain/worldPulse/settlementAlignment.js:19-21; src/domain/worldPulse/disposition.js:365-366, :530, :562; src/domain/spatial/moralDrift.js:27-30; src/domain/worldPulse/pulseKernel.js:2294-2295 (per a reader).
why: Developers may change alignment thinking nothing depends on it.
when: Correct the headers (grep list in the note's §11.3).

title: Disposition header miscounts its terms and names a retired field
what: The header says 'three blended terms' and lists four, and says the deity term reads the retired temperament field; the code reads the derived temper. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/disposition.js:9-27, :208-212 vs src/domain/worldPulse/deityAxes.js:26-33.
why: Misleads anyone tracing how a town's character is computed.
when: Correct the header.

title: The ruling seat does not count more than anyone else
what: Each NPC's weight is importance x the governing faction's power x 1.5; the last two factors are the same for every NPC and cancel in the average, so 'the seat of power colours the settlement more than a back-bench guild' does not happen. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/disposition.js:151-181, :418-435.
why: A town's alignment ignores who rules it; a map 'why' card would mis-explain the colour.
when: The note records it as a no-op; no fix given.

title: One scored NPC can set a whole town's conscience
what: NPCs with no scored word are skipped, so a single scored NPC sets the whole conscience or aggression term. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/disposition.js:171, :428.
why: A hamlet can read 'malicious' from one person; a choropleth (colour-by-region map) would show it as fact.
when: The note calls it a design question, not a bug.

title: Faith-by-alignment quadrant reads only the patrons' good/evil
what: The cohesion design says the quadrant comes from alignment closeness via culture distance; the owner's ruling 3 says faith war is distance across both axes; the code reads only the difference in the two patrons' evil score, so 'schism' can never occur. Host: docs/DESIGN_COHESION_WEAVE.md:25-28; docs/DESIGN_REALM_DIRECTIVES.md:166-172; src/domain/worldPulse/sacredClaim.js:121; src/domain/worldPulse/generosityKernel.js:333.
why: A religion lens must draw three classes, not four; the documents and the ruling describe something the code does not run.
when: Owner to decide which reading is meant (item 25d).

title: Two towns with no gods are treated as 'respectable rivals' in giving
what: A pair with no deities reads respectable_rival in generosity, scaling every conscience term by 0.95 on a born world; sacred-claim guards against this, generosity does not. Host: src/domain/spatial/cohesionWeave.js:53; src/domain/worldPulse/generosityKernel.js:414, :700; src/domain/worldPulse/sacredClaim.js:39-49.
why: Silent 5% damping of every relief decision on fresh worlds.
when: The note records it; the guard in sacredClaim.js is the model it points to.

title: Natural enemies refuse aid less readily, not more
what: The refuse threshold is 0.12 x hysteresis divided by the gate, so natural enemies (gate 0.55) need a larger withhold (0.218) to refuse and 'brothers' (1.25) a smaller one (0.096); the comment says the opposite. Bites only with seated deities. Host: src/domain/spatial/generosityEV.js:479-494; src/domain/spatial/cohesionWeave.js:49-54.
why: Relief arcs on the map go the wrong way between enemy and allied faiths.
when: The note records it as inverted; no fix given.

title: Two different 'rulers' for the same town
what: Alignment and faith read the governing seat; generosity takes the highest-power faction, which the faith code measured as the wrong faction on 36.7% of fresh settlements. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/generosityKernel.js:303-313; src/domain/worldPulse/religionLegitimacy.js:226-238.
why: Two systems disagree on who rules; a map naming 'the ruler' would contradict one of them.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Economic-base lens is always 'mixed'
what: Its three source keys have no writer, so every settlement reads 'mixed'. Host: src/domain/spatial/cohesionWeave.js:258-269.
why: A cohesion input that never varies.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Moral drift fades far faster than designed
what: Each tick the stored, already-faded drift is multiplied again by 0.92 to the power of all ticks since the last act, so fading compounds: half-life about 3.6 weeks instead of about 8.3, gone after 8 silent weeks instead of about 32 (measured by running the host function). Host: src/domain/spatial/moralDrift.js:218-224, :251-254.
why: A town's bad deeds vanish from its character in two months; a map time scrub replaying the designed curve would be wrong.
when: Item 25e asks the owner: keep the value at the last act so it does not compound.

title: Moral drift freezes in the default preset with war on
what: The ledger advances only when beliefs are active or a web-war atrocity happened this tick; only RR among raiding presets is omniscient, so in RR on canon with the war layer lit a raid-born drift does not fade between raids, and stays forever if the war layer is turned off. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/pulseKernel.js:2296, :2341-2350; src/domain/worldPulse/beliefMap.js:204-209; src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js:953, :996, :1073, :1404-1408, :720-730.
why: Permanent stain from one raid in the default preset.
when: Item 25e asks whether drift should decay every tick regardless of the belief gate.

title: Deceived towns drift toward evil, not toward their deceiver
what: The spatial design says a deceived good actor drifts toward the manipulator's alignment; the code drifts every unjust instigator toward malice and lawlessness. Host: docs/PHASE55_SPATIAL_ENGINE_DESIGN.md:514-517; src/domain/spatial/moralDrift.js:145-156.
why: Document and code disagree on direction.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Changing NPC alignment or institutions does not change a town's character
what: The spine requires mechanisms to move a town's character through NPC alignment, roster and institutions; the derived read never reads the NPC alignment word or institutions, and moral drift is a separate settlement accumulator (the parallel stock the requirement calls a defect). Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_SPINE.md:84-92; src/domain/worldPulse/disposition.js:112-128, :568-593; src/domain/worldPulse/moralMartialLean.js:143-163.
why: The design's own rule is broken; edits a DM makes to NPC alignment do not show on the map.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Corruption is named as an input and is not one
what: Corruption is listed as an alignment input but is not read (note §3.6).
why: A 'why' card would cite a cause that has no effect.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Three ways to compute a town's character, four lookup tables
what: The W0 axes, the faith conduct plane and the war seat books' fallback (law 0.5, malice 0.5 - 0.35 x conscience) each derive character; four archetype tables disagree; nothing reconciles them, though requirement 13 names W0 as the read. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/warSeatBooks.js:298-300.
why: Different systems see different characters; a fourth on the map side would make it worse.
when: The note records it; the map must call the host selector, not reimplement (§9.3 item 14).

title: Deity values used where the design says settlement values
what: The peace press, the quadrant and fidelity noise read patron axes; the spine requires the town's own two-axis read, and the selector header promises fidelity noise will widen to settlement alignment ('Wave A'), not done. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/peaceTermsAppraisal.js:86-104; src/domain/worldPulse/fidelityNoise.js:65-72; src/domain/worldPulse/settlementAlignment.js:20-21; docs/DESIGN_FP_SPINE.md:79-88.
why: A godless town's character never reaches these systems.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: 'Already live' oath price is only half live
what: The war-convenience document calls the lawfulness price in war termination and momentum 'ALREADY LIVE'; the momentum call is live in DC/FS on canon, the war-termination call is dark (warTerminationEnabled false in FS, absent elsewhere). Host: docs/DESIGN_WAR_CONVENIENCE_AND_TRIBUTE.md:646-651; src/domain/worldPulse/momentum.js:1265; src/domain/worldPulse/warTermination.js:745, :144.
why: Overstates what runs.
when: Correct the document.

title: Seeded NPC alignment word is read by nothing lit, and lacks chaotic good
what: No lit engine reads it; its vocabulary lacks chaotic_good though towns and deities can be chaotic-good; characterConsumers calls it a cache for two dark systems. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/npcAgency.js:161-170; src/domain/npc/characterConsumers.js:518-524.

when: The note records it; no fix given.

why: Armies and fleets do not choose routes by danger; a patrol or encounter map cannot show alignment-shaped army routes.

title: The good giver's charity exception is hard-coded off
what: Hard-coded false.
why: Designed behaviour that never fires.

why: Designed behaviour that never fires.

title: The humanitarian evidence door has no consumer

why: Designed behaviour that never fires.

why: Replacement NPCs never match the town.
when: The note records it as a seam.

title: Faction alignment for NPC circulation is never supplied

why: NPC circulation ignores faction character.

title: One moral ladder spelled two ways
what: conquestIntent says its bands are copied from the war seat books; the seat books say 'merciful', the intent and razing lanes say 'benevolent'. Both lanes dark. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/conquestIntent.js:64-71; src/domain/worldPulse/warSeatBooks.js:321-326.

when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Paradigm catalog says it has no consumers; four modules import it
what: Host: src/domain/npc/paradigmAxisCatalog.js:4-9, :78.

title: Founding an institution never needs a proposal
what: Founding severity peaks at 0.64, below the 0.78 proposal threshold, so a founding always applies itself even when major changes require proposals; abolition reaches it only at 0.95 or more. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/moralInstitutionPressure.js:347, :361, :508, :527.

title: 'Converts' in faith prescription means every linked neighbour
what: The name implies converted towns; the code presses every carrier-linked neighbour (note §5.1).
why: A map label using the host's word would mislead.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Coherence fold says migration has nowhere to go; M4 does
what: The fold says the migration menu is empty in every shipped world because nothing writes the route network; the M4 dispatch ranks destinations by the digest's path cost (the frozen travel table), not the route network. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_COHERENCE_FOLD.md:339; src/domain/worldPulse/migrationKernel.js:469-474.

what: The roads module gives a bold traveller risk tolerance 0.9 and a coward 0.35 and uses it correctly to decide refusal, but passes the same number to the route chooser, where it multiplies the danger surcharge, so the bold traveller avoids danger most and the coward least; the return leg uses the frozen value too. Lit with roadsEnabled on canon (RR, DC, LR, FS).
